title: request-fate-map-and-debugging-scenarios
content:
Purpose:
This working doc outlines a new console view pattern we are calling the "Request Fate Map" — a compact, horizontally-scoped visualization that shows the different terminal and intermediary outcomes for a single request or request cohort and provides jump-offs for targeted debugging (timelines, raw payload, model trace, infra metrics). Goal is to reduce time-to-root-cause for errors (esp. timeouts, 5xx, and model-level failures) by surfacing likely failure modes and the minimum useful next action for an engineer or SRE.

Context and motivation:
- Current investigator/triage surfaces are great for full-session debugging but are heavy and require multiple clicks to get the causal picture for a single failing request.
- On-call engineers often need a quick one-panel answer: was this client issue, network, capacity, model inference error, or a downstream service?
- We want a view that works both for single request debugging and aggregated cohort exploration (e.g., 95th percentile timeouts this hour).

High-level concept:
- The fate map is a Sankey-like horizontal lane showing the life of a request: ingress -> routing -> infra execution -> model exec -> post-processing -> downstream callouts -> final status.
- Each lane node is tagged with: count (if cohort), p95 latency, error rate, and primary error class (timeout, 5xx, model-error, fallback).
- Edges show proportions (thin/thick) and clickable to pivot into detailed traces filtered to that path.
- Hover state surfaces quick diagnostic hints (e.g., "KV cache hit rate 7% -> expected slower p95", "GPU OOM spikes at t+0.3s").

Wireframe notes (sketch -> components):
1) Top header: request id or cohort selector, timeframe, quick filters (model, region, deployment type)
2) Fate map canvas (center)
   - Lanes (columns): Ingress -> Router -> Queue/Batch -> Serving Node -> Model Exec -> Postprocessor -> Downstream -> Final Status
   - Node card: small rectangle with icon + 3 micro-metrics stacked (count/pct, p95 latency, error %). Clicking opens a right rail.
   - Edge click: opens mini-timeline focused on that slice (showing token timing if model exec).
3) Right rail (contextual debugging pane):
   - Summary band: reason-candidate (highest probability root cause), suggested next action (e.g., replay at lower batch size, switch to fallback model, increase timeout), confidence score
   - Tabs: Timeline | Logs | Raw payload | Model trace | Related incidents | Automated replay controls
   - Quick actions: create incident, flag for rollout, run synthetic replicate, open capacity view
4) Bottom panel: cohort heatmap for the selected timeframe showing density of failures by region/model/version

Example flows (user stories):
- On-call SRE sees spike in 5xx for region-us-west: opens cohort -> fate map shows most edges funnel to "Serving Node -> Model Exec -> Model-error" with high p95 at model exec. Right rail suggests "Model variant fallback active? check quantization profile" and a quick action to rollback to previous model version.
- Developer investigates single request with timeout: fate map shows request routed to cold node (queue/ batch long tail). Hover suggests "Autoscale policy not triggered; backlog length 42 at t-5m" and action to open dedicated capacity panel.

Backlog grooming items (prioritized):
- RF-1: Implement fate map backend endpoint (aggregated path traces). Estimate: 3 sprint days. Priority: high. Notes: requires sampling trace schema and computing edge weights server-side.
- RF-2: Right rail prototype with automated root-cause heuristics (pattern rules + simple bayesian scoring). Estimate: 5 sprint days. Priority: high.
- RF-3: Edge-hover quick hints integration with metrics store (Prometheus/TSDB). Estimate: 2 sprint days. Priority: medium.
- RF-4: Cohort selector UI and ad-hoc query language. Estimate: 4 sprint days. Priority: medium.
- RF-5: Integrate with canary/rollout system for one-click rollback. Estimate: 5 sprint days. Priority: low.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Fate map renders for selected request id and for cohorts (timebox to last hour).
- Each node shows count, p95, error% and edges reflect distribution; clicking an edge filters traces in the right rail.
- Right rail recommends at least one next action for timeouts and 5xx with a confidence string.
- Hover state shows at least two inline diagnostic hints pulled from metrics/logs.

Design tradeoffs / open questions:
- Level of aggregation: lane granularity (should we split model exec into tokenize/kv-cache/load/compute?). Tradeoff: too many nodes increase cognitive load. Proposed: two-mode view — compact vs expanded.
- Probabilistic root-cause: how much to automate? Risk of false suggestions -> must surface confidence and allow easy dismissal.
- Performance cost of computing fate map for large cohorts — propose pre-aggregations for 1m/5m intervals and on-demand partial recompute.
- Data retention and privacy: show only internal ids and scrub PII from raw payload previews. Confirm with security/compliance.

Mockup text (quick sketch, ascii):
[HEADER] Request: abc123 | cohort: timeouts last 1h | mdl: redwood-7B | region: us-west
[CANVAS]
Ingress  -> Router -> Queue  -> Serving -> Model Exec -> Postproc -> Downstream -> Status
  [10k]     [9.8k]    [320]     [300]      [210]        [205]       [4]      [200 ok / 110 timeout / 10 5xx]
  (hover Queue) -> "avg wait 420ms, p95 2.1s, backlog 42"
  (click Serving->Model Exec edge) -> Right rail opens: Timeline tab shows burst of token-latency at t+0.5s correlating with GPU swap

Operational notes for backend team:
- Traces should include minimal schema: request_id, path_nodes[], timestamps[], outcome, model_version, node_tags[]; path_nodes should be normalized keys to enable aggregations.
- Implement a sampling policy: always capture full trace for 1/1000 requests and aggregated metrics for all (counts/p95/error%)
- Add label propagation for fallback decisions and routing policy to be surfaceable on nodes (e.g., fallback=true, routed-by=latency-policy)

Open action items (assigned):
- Ava: draft initial API contract for aggregated path traces and circulate to infra (due 2024-11-12)
- Ravi: prototype right-rail heuristics ruleset (due 2024-11-19)
- Sofia: coordinate with security on payload scrubbing policy (due 2024-11-07)
- Jordan: rough hi-fi mock in Figma for compact/expanded modes (due 2024-11-15)

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Could add a "what-if" toggle to simulate lower batching or smaller seq-len to show impact on p95 — useful for developers when testing model changes.
- Consider small CTA for customer success: export cohort summary for a support ticket.
- Keep the color language minimal (red/orange/gray) and ensure colorblind-safe palette.

References and related work:
- Linked investigation: JIRA-OPS-987 (large timeout spike, aug 2024)
- Prior art: internal "failure-demuxer" doc (see related folder), and a visualization prototype from console/ux lab (PR #412).

Next steps:
1) Sync with infra and telemetry to confirm feasibility of path aggregation (target meeting: 2024-11-01).
2) Kickoff 1-week spike: backend API + sample UI in storybook to validate perf.
3) Run 2 user interviews with on-call SRE and one product engineer to validate heuristics and suggested actions.

End of doc.
